clue.text: Second best hoot

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: An owl's call is ranked second best in some contest of hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally both words describe a person or thing found hilariously funny, as in 'she was a real laugh'.

clue.text: Commander has to approve captain

blocks.note: CO is short for Commanding Officer
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: A senior officer must sign off on a ship's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: Captain James Cook, the eighteenth-century explorer of the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cook was a famous British naval explorer who held the rank of captain, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Pepsi Cola, refreshment of bishops

indicators.note: refreshing something renews and remakes it, so the drink's letters are made over in new order

blocks.note: the soft drink's name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Clergymen at a church gathering are served a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcopal church is governed by bishops; the adjective comes from the Greek word for overseer.

clue.text: Skirt worn by favourite

blocks.note: a mini is a short skirt
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A skirt is modelled by somebody's preferred person.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion was originally a royal darling or pet courtier, a servile dependant who enjoys a patron's favour.

clue.text: Rover, in search of pleasure, takes false silver back and forth

indicators.note: going back means the preceding words are read from right to left

blocks.note: a bad cheque or coin is a false one
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to go forth is to go out

explanation.surface: A wanderer pursuing fun carries counterfeit silver to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back and forth' reads as one phrase meaning to and fro, but it splits: 'back' reverses false silver, then 'forth' adds its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a person who roams from place to place seeking amusement and social activity.

clue.text: Get huge pot and clear out with financial compensation

indicators.note: to clear out is to turn things upside down, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A departing executive scoops a big pot of money and walks away with a payoff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a fair picture of the answer, a big payout to a sacked boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden parachute is a generous severance payment contracted for a senior executive who loses the job.

clue.text: Duchamp's first on a platform, initially talking shop with Hans Arp, Man Ray et al.

definitions.text: Hans Arp, Man Ray et al.

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the artist's name is kept
initially points to the opening letters of the following words only

blocks.note: the opening letter of the French artist's name
A can mean on, as in twice a day
a dais is a raised platform
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Duchamp holds forth on a stage, talking shop with fellow artists Arp and Man Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: Duchamp was himself one of the group, so the whole clue is a fair picture; 'on' giving A follows the 'per' sense, as in once a week.
explanation.definitionFit: Arp and Man Ray were leading members of Dada, the early twentieth-century anti-art movement.

clue.text: Central heating on stream as a kind of offering?

indicators.note: central asks for the letter at the exact middle of the following word

blocks.note: a burn is a Scottish word for a small stream
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: Home heating fed by running water is offered as a sort of gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the stream first: the middle letter of heating is put on, that is after, the stream. The question mark flags that the definition only completes a phrase: a burnt offering.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnt offering is a sacrifice consumed by fire on an altar, so the word describes one kind of sacrifice.

clue.text: Nice suntan all over? Most weird!

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is tanned evenly over the whole body, which is most odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means strange in an unsettling way, so the superlative is the strangest or eeriest of all.

clue.text: There's not an island left that's not based on fact

blocks.note: taken as written
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A claim that no island remains is dismissed as untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notional exists only as an idea or estimate rather than as a real, verified thing.

clue.text: Frank guide

blocks.note: first meaning: straightforward and outspoken
second meaning: to steer or show the way

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter makes Frank look like a man's name, as though he were the guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for blunt honest speech and a verb for steering or managing someone.

clue.text: Chummy's apt to be tight

blocks.note: close friends are chummy; the 's stands for is
fitting means suitable or apt

explanation.surface: A friendly person tends to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight is slang for drunk, which the surface plays on, but here it describes clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-fitting garments hug the body, which is what tight clothes do.

clue.text: Car was effective for one not needing instructor

blocks.note: auto is short for automobile
a remedy that did act was one that worked

explanation.surface: A car proved useful to somebody learning to drive without lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An autodidact is a self-taught person who learns without a teacher.

clue.text: Try to get information from shoe

blocks.note: first meaning: to question someone persistently
second meaning: a light flat shoe such as a plimsoll or court shoe

explanation.walkthrough: In British use a pump is a plimsoll or a light dancing shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to quiz them for facts, and a pump is also a kind of soft flat footwear.

clue.text: Pitiful epic that failed

indicators.note: something that failed has fallen apart, so the letters before it are reassembled

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand film or poem that flopped is judged woeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means arousing pity, or contemptibly poor, both senses of pitiful.

clue.text: I seem prepared to hold singer responsible for missions

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the preceding letters are rearranged
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged
a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice

explanation.surface: Someone appears ready to detain a singer who is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomatic missions are embassies, the official delegations or premises of a foreign government.

clue.text: In a stew, in a stew, in a stew? Good!

indicators.note: being in a stew means being in a muddle, so the preceding letters are thrown into confusion

blocks.note: the letters of these words are rearranged
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone repeats that they are flustered, then cheerily declares it good.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase plays three roles: the definition, the letters to rearrange, and the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew means being agitated or anxious, and sweating is informal for worrying nervously.

clue.text: Disciple with heart of gold in bloom

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only its central letters are kept
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a bloom is a flower
the two central letters of the four

explanation.surface: An adherent carries a golden-centred blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle pair goes after the first letter of bloom's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower is someone who adheres to a teacher or cause, which is what a disciple does.

clue.text: Party clobber

blocks.note: first meaning: a lively social gathering
second meaning: to hit hard

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang clobber also means clothing or gear, so 'Party clobber' reads as an outfit for a do.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word names a festive celebration and also, as a verb, means to strike with a heavy blow.

clue.text: Risk associated with fish shop

blocks.note: a bet is a risk or gamble
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A gamble tied up with a fishmonger's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish shop' looks like a chippy, but shop is a verb: British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone, in British slang, is to inform on them to the police, which is a form of treachery.

clue.text: Hobbies to interest these hobbyists?

blocks.note: surface reading: pastimes that appeal to people who have pastimes
setter's reading: a hobby is a small falcon, so these are people keen on spotting such creatures

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to go in a circle about pastimes, but the hobby is also a small falcon of the British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdwatchers are enthusiasts who observe wild species such as the hobby falcon for pleasure.

clue.text: Princess in Edwardian attire

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the last four letters of the first word and the first of the second

explanation.surface: A royal lady dressed in period costume from the early 1900s.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, Princess of Wales, was the most famous princess of that name.

clue.text: Wilder make-up unit?

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the American comic actor Wilder
second meaning: a unit of genetic make-up

explanation.walkthrough: Gene Wilder starred in Willy Wonka and Young Frankenstein. Make-up suggests cosmetics in a dressing room, but here it is the body's inherited constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is the forename of the actor Wilder and also the basic unit of heredity in DNA.

clue.text: Expression of grief about note on sausage

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the cry of grief is read backwards

blocks.note: alas is a cry of sorrow
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cry of sadness over a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly seasoned Italian sausage, usually eaten sliced and cold.

clue.text: University given tribute for being elevated

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
someone praised has been paid tribute

explanation.surface: A university is honoured for having been promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Upraised means raised up or lifted high, which is to say elevated.

clue.text: Suppress onset of laughter in unfamiliar setting

indicators.note: the onset of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is kept
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: strange means unfamiliar; setting marks it as the surround
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone stifles the first giggles in an odd environment.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of laughter goes inside after the first five letters of the synonym for unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle a thing is to stifle or check it, as in strangling a cry, so it means suppress.

clue.text: Country infiltrated by skinhead's obsequious subordinates

indicators.note: something infiltrated has an intruder slipped inside it

blocks.note: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula
read as skin's head: the opening letter of skin

explanation.surface: A nation is penetrated by a shaven-headed thug's fawning lackeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinhead's reads as a shaven thug, but split it: the head of skin is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men always agree with their boss, being sycophantic underlings who never voice dissent.
